title: Right to Information
description: Understanding Nepal's constitutional provisions for Right to Information (RTI) and its implementation.

sections.title: What is the Right to Information?
sections.content: The Right to Information (RTI) empowers citizens to request and receive information held by public bodies. It promotes transparency, accountability, and informed civic participation. In Nepal, the Constitution and RTI Act establish mechanisms for public access to non-sensitive government records.
keyPoints: Citizens can request information from public authorities
Legal timelines exist for providing information

sections.title: Legal Framework in Nepal
sections.content: RTI is grounded in constitutional guarantees and implemented through legislation defining procedures, exemptions, and appeal mechanisms. Public agencies must designate information officers and maintain proactive disclosures to minimize individual requests.
keyPoints: Constitutional basis for access to information

sections.title: Request Process and Exemptions
sections.content: Citizens submit a written or electronic request specifying the information sought. Authorities must respond within a stipulated period—either providing the information, denying with reason, or extending time under defined circumstances. Exempt categories typically include national security, personal privacy, and ongoing investigations.

sections.title: Impact and Implementation Challenges
sections.content: RTI has improved public oversight of budgets, procurement, and service delivery. Challenges remain: limited awareness, bureaucratic delays, incomplete record digitization, and overuse of exemption claims. Strengthening capacity and public education can enhance effectiveness.

sections.title: Historical Context of RTI
sections.content: RTI emerged from broader democratic reforms emphasizing accountability and anti‑corruption. Progressive jurisprudence clarified disclosure duties and narrowed broad secrecy claims.

sections.title: Practical Applications
sections.content: Civic groups use RTI to audit local project spending, verify procurement fairness, and monitor service delivery quality—creating feedback loops for administrative improvement.

sections.title: Implementation Gaps
sections.content: Inconsistent record digitization, limited metadata standards, and variable officer training produce response delays and quality variance. Proactive data catalogs remain underdeveloped.

sections.title: Case Study: Local Budget Transparency
sections.content: A community organization files RTI requests on a stalled infrastructure project, uncovering procurement delays and prompting administrative corrective measures and public disclosure updates.

sections.title: Future Outlook
sections.content: Next steps include machine‑readable proactive publication, integrated request tracking dashboards, strengthened sanctions for wrongful denial, and public digital literacy expansion.

sections.title: Case Study: Applying Concepts
sections.content: A practical scenario demonstrates how principles from "Right to Information" operate in real life. Consider a local authority decision challenged for compliance with constitutional norms. Analyze actors involved, legal basis, and remedy pathways to understand implementation dynamics.
